name: Three Black Crows
description: A three-candle bearish continuation or reversal pattern consisting of three consecutive large bearish candles. Each candle opens within or near the previous candle's body and closes progressively lower, with small or no lower wicks. Signals strong and sustained selling pressure over multiple sessions.

body_rules.candle_1: large bearish body; first crow, ideally forming at or near the end of an uptrend or consolidation
body_rules.candle_2: large bearish body; opens within candle 1's body and closes below candle 1's close
body_rules.candle_3: large bearish body; opens within candle 2's body and closes below candle 2's close
body_rules.progression: each candle should close lower than the previous; bodies should be of similar size

wick_rules.lower_wicks: should be small or nonexistent on all three candles; long lower wicks indicate buying attempts and weaken the pattern
wick_rules.upper_wicks: small upper wicks are acceptable and indicate that rallies within each session were sold into

context_requirement: most powerful when forming at the end of an uptrend or at a major resistance level; also valid as a continuation signal after a breakdown from consolidation; less reliable if forming deep into an extended downtrend (exhaustion risk)
volume_requirement: volume should be consistently high across all three candles or progressively increasing; declining volume on the third candle is a warning sign of weakening momentum
agent_rules: Confirm the pattern forms at or near a resistance level, supply zone, or after a breakdown of consolidation
Enter short after the third candle closes or at the open of candle 4
Stop loss above the high of candle 1 or above the midpoint of candle 1's body
Three black crows with long lower wicks are considered weakened crows — reduce position size or skip
If the third candle is significantly smaller than the first two, momentum may be fading — be cautious
Avoid chasing this pattern if price is already overextended below key moving averages
Volume consistency or increase across all three candles is a strong confirmation factor
